newsitem.title: LATVIA: IMF WELCOMES NEW ESTONIA BANK ADEQUACY RATIOS.
newsitem.headline: IMF WELCOMES NEW ESTONIA BANK ADEQUACY RATIOS.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Wednesday welcomed new capital adequacy ratios for Estonian banks, which have been raised from eight to 10 percent, and said the rise may dampen the growth of credit.
But IMF Estonia and Latvia resident representative Dimitri Demekas told Reuters that the move would not hit Estonia's economic growth.
"We are happy and this (a rise in the ratios) is part of the programme that we agreed with Estonia," Demekas said.

The Estonian central bank earlier announced that it has increased bank capital adequacy ratios and said this would prevent banks from taking additional risks in lending to gain a competitive advantage over other banks.
"It may have an small curbing effect on the rate of growth of credit but at the same time it will boost confidence in the Estonian banking system," Demekas added.
"I do not expect a dampening of economic growth," he added.
Several Estonian officials have said they were worried about the growth of banks' lending and that this was fuelling what an over-heating Estonian economy.
Credit to the private sector by commercial banks grew by 70 percent in 1996 compared with economic growth of between three and five percent.
The previous capital adequacy ratio of eight percent was the minimum mandated under by Basel committee, which draws up rules for commercial banks all over the world.
In most transition economies, the capital adequacy ratios are higher.
